items.followUp: Define boiling and state two factors that affect the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface below its boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a liquid changes into vapour from its surface below its boiling point.

rubric.why: Raising the temperature increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing temperature increases the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Increasing the exposed surface area allows more particles to escape at a time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing the exposed surface area increases the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Faster wind carries vapour away, while lower humidity allows more vapour to enter the air.
rubric.description: Effect of wind speed or humidity
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing wind speed or lowering humidity increases evaporation.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface at a temperature below its boiling point.
An increase in temperature increases the rate of evaporation because more particles have enough energy to escape.
An increase in the exposed surface area increases the rate of evaporation.
A higher wind speed increases evaporation by carrying vapour away; lower humidity also increases evaporation.

items.followUp: Write the empirical and molecular formulae of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆.

rubric.why: The simplest whole-number ratio of carbon to hydrogen in benzene is 1:1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving CH as the empirical formula.

rubric.why: A benzene molecule contains six carbon atoms and six hydrogen atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving C₆H₆ as the molecular formula.

items.followUp: Define a molecule and give an example of a diatomic molecule.

rubric.why: A molecule is the smallest particle of an element or compound that can exist independently and retain its chemical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a molecule as the smallest particle that can exist independently and retains the substance's properties.

rubric.why: Each listed example contains three atoms in one molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid triatomic molecule, such as H₂O, O₃ or CO₂.

modelAnswer: A molecule is the smallest particle of an element or compound that can exist independently and retain its chemical properties.
Water, H₂O, is an example of a triatomic molecule.

items.followUp: An element has atomic number 12. Write the number of electrons in its K, L and M shells.

rubric.why: The K shell contains two electrons in the distribution for an element with atomic number 17.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the K shell contains 2 electrons.

rubric.why: The remaining electrons are distributed as 8 in the L shell and 7 in the M shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving both L = 8 and M = 7 electrons.

modelAnswer: For a neutral atom, number of electrons = atomic number = 17.
K shell = 2 electrons; L shell = 8 electrons; M shell = 7 electrons.
